title: Annotatio II §.V: Marbach Senior confirms with harsher theses — human nature called God; Fechtius reports
pass_a_gloss: and confirmed and defended by Marbach the Elder also by other similar and more absurd propositions, by which he dared to affirm that Christ's Human Nature can rightly be called even God Himself — which the most celebrated Fechtius himself reports in the Supplement to Ecclesiastical History, page 30; compare Hospinian, Concordia discordans, chapter 55;
pass_b_english: Marbach the Elder then confirmed and defended it with further like — and even more absurd — propositions, daring to say Christ's human nature can rightly be called God Himself.
So Fechtius reports in his Supplement to Ecclesiastical History, p. 30 (cf. Hospinian, Concordia discordans, ch. 55).
source_text: & à Marbachio Sen. aliis etiam propositionibus similibus & absurdioribus confirmatam defensamque, quibus Humanam Christi Naturam vel DEum ipsum rectè dici posse, ausus est affirmare, id quod ipse Celeberr. Fechtius refert, in Supplem. Historiae Eccl. pag. 30. Conf. Hospin. Concord. discord. cap. 55.;

lemmas.latin: Humanam Christi Naturam vel DEum ipsum
lemmas.gloss: Christ's Human Nature or even God Himself

choices.why: vel intensifying; Fecht's reported extreme predication
rejected: or God as alternative person only
